fact_text: A trending market makes higher highs and higher lows, while a sideways market stays inside a range without breaking its highs or lows.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)

fact_text: The analyst said markets are about 30% trending and about 70% sideways most of the time.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)

fact_text: On 5 May 2025 the KSE-100 was trading sideways inside a range after making a high, with no clear trend in place.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)

fact_text: Inside a range the analyst's approach is to sell near the range ceiling and buy near the range floor, and to wait when price sits in the middle with no clear edge.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)

fact_text: A range breakout counts as valid only with heavy volume and a strong candle; the analyst said the move should be confirmed before following it.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)

fact_text: Falling volume inside a range was read as fading investor interest, so the range is more likely to persist until volume returns.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)

fact_text: A trading range is defined by marking the high where price was rejected and the lower level where buying appeared, then watching both boundaries.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'What 99% of Traders Don't Know About PSX Trading in Sideways Markets' (YouTube, 2025-05-05)
